newsitem.title: USA: CBOT nearby wheat ends up on stocks ideas.
newsitem.headline: CBOT nearby wheat ends up on stocks ideas.

text.p: CBOT nearby wheat contracts closed higher on short covering and position squaring before the release Monday of USDA's quarterly grain and oilseed stocks report, traders said.
An average of analysts' estimates ahead of the report pegged the U.S. wheat supply as of September 1 at 1.767 billion bushels, below 1.881 billion a year ago.

Traders also said wheat was in a seasonal upswing after sliding recently amid a slowdown in exports and increased competition for export business from other producers. Also, wheat has been forming a technical base, a technician said.
First support in Dec was $4.26-1/4 and first resistance was $4.32-3/4, they said.

Commercial stopping of deliveries on the expired September and commercial bull spreading also boosted the December. Continental Grain stopped all of the 195,000 bushels posted Friday for delivery and also bull spread 600,000 bushels of December/March, the traders said.
Wheat closed 2-1/4 cents per bushel higher to 2-1/2 lower, with December up 2-1/4 at $4.31-1/2.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 10,000 contracts, down from 11,008 Thursday, according to the CBOT.

In wheat options, Paine Webber bought 200 December $4.40 calls at 9-3/4 cents, Continental Grain sold 400 December $4.50 calls at 6-1/2 to 6-3/4 cents and Prudential Securities bought 200 December $4.10 puts and sold 200 March $3.80 puts at 1/4 cent, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 8,000 contracts, down from 8,720 Thursday.
